hero.headline: The AI chip selloff spreads to Asia: Korea's KOSPI falls 6.2% as Samsung drops nearly 10%.
hero.dek: Every story on FIOPO is traced to where it lands: your fuel, your rent, your savings, your job. Here is how today's biggest story travels.

chain.label: The event
chain.text: On Tuesday the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 7.9% and the Nasdaq 1.48% to 23,733.54. Nvidia fell 5.86% a day after its 31.5% jump, Micron 11.01% and AMD 8.86%.

chain.label: The trigger
chain.text: Investors questioned the returns on debt funded AI data center spending and Nvidia's governance after Jensen Huang's reinstatement, AP and Al Jazeera report. Fears of new US tariffs added pressure.

chain.label: The world
chain.text: On Wednesday the KOSPI fell 6.2% to 4,697.51, Taiwan's Taiex 5% and the Nikkei 2.8%. Samsung fell 9.9% and SK Hynix 11.1%. In Europe, Infineon fell 9.7% and ASML 5.6%, Saxo reports.

chain.label: The catch
chain.text: Not everything fell. The Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70 as money moved into health care and consumer stocks, and US consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 from 91.9.

chain.label: You
chain.text: The 10 year Treasury yield eased to 4.875% early Wednesday from 4.93%, Saxo says. Funds heavy in a few chip stocks are swinging hardest. PCE inflation lands at 8:30 a.m. ET.

hero.caption: Sources: AP, Al Jazeera, Saxo, Motley Fool via Yahoo Finance, Startup Fortune and the Conference Board, November 24 to 25, 2026. The chain itself is FIOPO analysis.

stories.headline: Chip stocks slump from New York to Seoul as AI doubts return.
stories.happened: On Tuesday the S&P 500 fell 0.50% to 7,201.09, its eighth loss in nine sessions, and the Nasdaq fell 1.48% to 23,733.54. The Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 7.9%. Nvidia fell 5.86%, Micron 11.01%, Intel 8.15% and AMD 8.86%, while Kohl's, Dollar Tree and Dick's Sporting Goods jumped after earnings.
stories.happening: On Wednesday Asia followed: the KOSPI fell 6.2%, the Taiex 5%, the Nikkei 2.8% to 57,011.62 and the Shanghai Composite 1.5% to its lowest in more than a year, AP reports. Samsung fell 9.9%, SK Hynix 11.1% and SoftBank Group 14.8%. India's Sensex rose 2.4%. Europe's STOXX 600 was down 0.7% in early trade and the DAX 1.3%, Saxo says. US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving.

could.text: Two days of 30% and 6% swings in one stock show how much of the market now rides on a handful of AI names. Wednesday's PCE report adds a second test.

you: Check how much of your retirement fund sits in the ten largest tech stocks; an S&P 500 fund is more concentrated than it looks.
Keep regular contributions on schedule rather than reacting to single day swings.
Money you need within two years belongs in savings or short Treasury bills, not in chip stocks.
stories.watch: PCE inflation at 8:30 a.m. ET Wednesday, then the Fed's Beige Book at 2 p.m. ET.

stories.headline: The US is preparing new tariffs on China, the EU and 14 other economies.
stories.happened: The Trump administration is expected to soon announce higher tariffs on 16 economies, including China and the EU, two people familiar with the matter told AP on Tuesday. The US Trade Representative is due to release results of monthslong Section 301 investigations into industrial subsidies in the coming days. Bloomberg and The Wall Street Journal reported the plans earlier.
stories.happening: The tariff levels were not clear and timing could still change, AP says. The White House says subsidized overproduction in those countries floods the US with cheap goods. The duties would come on top of 10% to 12.5% tariffs announced this year, and would replace broader April 2025 tariffs the Supreme Court struck down in February. The White House and USTR did not respond to AP. Trump met Xi Jinping in Shenzhen last week, and Xi is expected at the G20 in Florida next month.

odds.label: New Section 301 tariffs announced by Dec 25

could.note: FIOPO read for the next 30 days. Judgment, not fact.

you: Planning a big purchase of imported goods, such as appliances or electronics? Prices can rise once new tariffs take effect.
Run a small business that imports? Ask suppliers now how they would share any new duty.
Own funds with heavy exposure to exporters in China or Europe? Expect swings when the list is published.
stories.watch: USTR findings in the coming days.

stories.headline: Consumer confidence jumps to 103.3 as traders bet on a December Fed hike.
stories.happened: The Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose 11.4 points to 103.3 in November from 91.9, well above the 92.2 forecast. The expectations index rose to 83.6 and 12 month inflation expectations eased to 5.7%. Conference Board economist Fergus McCormick linked the gain to lower uncertainty after the midterm elections, while consumers still complained about high prices.
stories.happening: Futures put the odds of a quarter point Fed hike on December 9 at about 95% to 96%, with the rest on a half point, according to CME FedWatch data cited by Closing Look. The 10 year Treasury yield closed Tuesday at 4.93% and eased to 4.875% early Wednesday, Saxo says. Australia's October inflation came in at 4.9%, above the 4.7% forecast. US PCE inflation, income and spending, jobless claims and durable goods all arrive Wednesday.

could.text: A hot PCE reading would revive talk of a half point move.
could.note: Market odds from futures pricing, Closing Look citing CME FedWatch, November 24. Not a FIOPO call.

you: Carry a credit card balance? Pay down the highest rate card first; card rates follow the Fed.
Shopping for a mortgage? Ask about a rate lock before the December 9 decision.
Holding cash? Compare high yield savings rates, which tend to rise after hikes.
stories.watch: PCE inflation at 8:30 a.m. ET Wednesday.

sources.name: Conference Board via PR Newswire, Nov 24

stories.headline: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for about $41 billion in cash.
stories.happened: France's Sanofi agreed on November 24 to buy US drugmaker Insmed for $175 a share in cash, a total equity value of about $41.0 billion. The deal brings Brinsupri, a once daily pill for the lung disease non cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, which Sanofi says earned $1.09 billion through September 30, 2026, a little over a year after its US launch.
stories.happening: Both boards approved the deal, which needs Insmed shareholder and regulatory approval and is expected to close in the first half of 2027. Sanofi will fund it with debt and cash and expects it to add to earnings per share by the end of 2028. Insmed shares rose 14.13% on Tuesday, and Sanofi's shares were up 9.8% in Paris on Wednesday morning, Saxo reports.

could.text: A deal this size draws close review from regulators, but the two companies have little overlap in respiratory drugs.

you: Own Insmed shares? A cash offer usually caps the upside; read the shareholder vote materials when they arrive.
Taking Brinsupri? Ownership changes rarely affect prescriptions, but ask your pharmacy about any change in patient support programs.
Own a health care fund? Big pharma deals can lift other mid size biotech stocks on takeover hopes.

regions.covers: China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Southeast Asia
regions.headline: Shanghai stocks hit a more than one year low as Xiaomi's profit falls 68%.
regions.text: The Shanghai Composite fell 1.5% to 3,494.75 on Wednesday, its lowest in more than a year, while the KOSPI fell 6.2% and the Nikkei 2.8%, AP reports. Xiaomi said third quarter net profit fell 68% to 3.9 billion yuan as revenue slipped 5.2% to 107 billion yuan and smartphone shipments dropped 29.1%, City News Service reports.
regions.you: Own a China or Asia fund? Check its weight in chips and consumer electronics, the two areas under the most pressure this week.

sources.name: AP via KSAT, Asian markets, Nov 25

regions.covers: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka
regions.headline: India's Sensex jumps 2.4% to a six month high as the rest of Asia falls.
regions.text: The Sensex rose 2.4% on Wednesday to its highest in six months, AP reports, after markets were shut Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti. In morning trade it was up 1,736.10 points at 84,172.09, with foreign buying and gains in Infosys, HDFC Bank and Reliance, The Open Press reports. The rupee opened near 92.74 per dollar from 92.91.
regions.you: Investing in Indian funds? Big single day gains often follow holidays; add on a fixed schedule rather than chasing a rally.

sources.name: AP via KSAT, Asian markets, Nov 25

regions.headline: European chip stocks drop as German business confidence hits a two and a half year high.
regions.text: Europe's STOXX 600 fell 0.7% and Germany's DAX 1.3% early Wednesday, with Infineon down 9.7% and ASML 5.6%, Saxo reports. Germany's Ifo business climate index rose to 90.6, its highest since May 2023. The European Central Bank meets December 16 to 17, with markets expecting another rate hike, IC Markets says.
regions.you: Hold European stocks? Chip makers and banks are moving in opposite directions; check which side your fund leans toward.

regions.headline: Trump dismisses Iran's statements as mine claims in Hormuz continue.
regions.text: President Trump told Fox News that Iran's statements were "all BS" and suggested the US could resume strikes on Iranian targets after the end of the year, OilPrice.com reports. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, claims not independently verified. Brent settled up 2.27% at $91.40 on Tuesday and fell 1.4% to $87.50 on Wednesday, AP says.
regions.you: Shipping goods through the Gulf? Confirm insurance and routing with your carrier; mine claims can change war risk premiums quickly.

sources.name: AP via KSAT, Asian markets, Nov 25

regions.covers: Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, Sahel
regions.headline: Nigeria's central bank holds its key rate at 23%.
regions.text: The Central Bank of Nigeria kept its monetary policy rate at 23% on November 24 and held all other settings, citing a moderation in headline inflation, the News Agency of Nigeria and Parrot Nigeria report. In Cabo Verde, President José Maria Neves won 63.8% with 97% of provisional results counted, avoiding a runoff, The Rio Times reports.
regions.you: Borrowing or saving in naira? With the rate on hold, compare fixed deposit rates now before banks reprice.

sources.name: The Rio Times, Africa brief, Nov 24

regions.headline: Argentina's peso hits its weakest close in a year as Brazil's spending bill heads to Lula.
regions.text: The dollar closed at 1,592 pesos on Tuesday, the peso's weakest close in 12 months, after September economic activity fell 1.2% from a year earlier, The Rio Times reports. In Brazil the spending curbs bill, passed 353 to 128, now goes to President Lula, who has 15 working days to sign or veto it. Overdue household and company debt hit a record R$371.1 billion in the third quarter.
regions.you: Traveling to Argentina? A weaker peso stretches dollars further, but check card fees and official exchange rates before you go.

sources.name: The Rio Times, Argentina markets, Nov 24
The Rio Times, Latin American Pulse, Nov 25

sports.headline: Netflix leads the race for US rights to the 2030 World Cup.
sports.text: FIFA has moved US rights to the 2030 men's World Cup into a second round of bidding, with Netflix the clear leader, Inside World Football reported on November 25. Fox and Univision, bidding together, and Amazon are also in. FIFA is seeking $1.5 billion to $2 billion, against $485 million from Fox and $600 million from Telemundo for 2026.
sports.you: Expect more big sports events behind streaming subscriptions; check which services carry the games you watch before renewing.

sports.headline: DAZN and Viaplay win UEFA club rights in a new round of deals.
sports.text: UC3, the UEFA and European Football Clubs joint venture, named preferred bidders in 10 more markets for 2027 to 2031 on November 24, Broadband TV News reports. DAZN takes all three men's club competitions in Israel and Champions League rights in Australia, and Viaplay keeps the Champions League in Iceland. The deals start in July 2027.
sports.you: Follow European football abroad? Your local broadcaster may change in 2027, so watch for new subscription offers.

sports.headline: Dick's Sporting Goods jumps 14.59% after earnings.
sports.text: Shares of Dick's Sporting Goods rose 14.59% on November 24 after its quarterly report, one of several retailers, with Kohl's and Abercrombie, that gained on results as investors moved into consumer stocks, Closing Look reports.
sports.you: Buying gear for the holidays? Retailers reporting strong demand tend to offer fewer deep discounts, so compare prices early.

entertainment.headline: Ramayana jumps 35% on Tuesday at the Indian box office.
entertainment.text: Ramayana Part I earned Rs 15.98 crore net in India on Tuesday, November 24, up about 35% from Monday's Rs 11.83 crore, with the Hindi version contributing Rs 13.31 crore, Bollywood Hungama reports.
entertainment.you: Indian epics are getting long theater runs abroad too; check local listings before waiting for streaming.

entertainment.headline: Godzilla Minus Zero passes Rs 4 crore in India in five days.
entertainment.text: The Japanese film earned Rs 56 lakh net in India on November 24, up 37.5% from Monday, bringing its five day total to about Rs 4.05 crore, Bollywood Hungama reports. Almost all of that came from the Japanese language version.
entertainment.you: Subtitled films are drawing real audiences in India; look for original language screenings if you prefer them.

innovation.headline: Anthropic shares fall below their $83 IPO price four days after listing.
innovation.text: Anthropic closed at $81.90 on November 24, down 6.54% and below its $83 IPO price, Closing Look reports, after briefly reaching $115 on its first day of trading, AP says. Bloomberg reported the shares broke below the IPO price in premarket trading. Gartner forecasts global AI investment of $2.7 trillion this year, Al Jazeera reports.
innovation.you: Thinking of buying a hot new listing? First week prices swing widely; wait for the first earnings report before committing much money.

sources.name: AP via KSAT, Asian markets, Nov 25

innovation.headline: Samsung plans to raise its Xi'an NAND output about fivefold.
innovation.text: Samsung plans to lift capacity for its V9 NAND memory at its Xi'an plant in China from about 10,000 to about 50,000 wafers a month, City News Service reported on November 25.
innovation.you: Shopping for laptops or phones? More memory supply over time usually means cheaper storage upgrades.

innovation.headline: Maersk orders 12 ultra large container ships for 2030 delivery.
innovation.text: Maersk has ordered 12 ultra large container ships for delivery in 2030 and 2031, linked by industry reports to China's Hengli Heavy Industries, City News Service reports. Brokers estimate about $229 million per vessel.
innovation.you: Shipping costs feed into the price of imported goods; bigger ships aim to cut cost per container over time.

travel.headline: Lake Balaton, Hungary: a lake holiday without Como's crowds.
travel.text: Lonely Planet named Lake Balaton one of its most underrated places for 2027, for summer festivals, castles and lavender fields, as an alternative to Lake Como.
travel.you: Planning summer 2027? Look at lakeside towns now, and pay in forint rather than accepting a card conversion to dollars.

travel.headline: St. Augustine, Florida: Spanish streets without a transatlantic flight.
travel.text: Lonely Planet's 2027 underrated list includes St. Augustine for centuries of history and Spanish style streets that give a European feel on a domestic trip.
travel.you: Want old Europe on a short break? A domestic trip skips passports and long haul fares. Check the official visitor site for events before you book.

travel.headline: The dollar buys more in Argentina and Brazil than in a year.
travel.text: Argentina's peso closed at 1,580 per dollar on November 20, its weakest in at least 12 months, and Brazil's real closed near 5.93, its weakest since January 2025. Lonely Planet's 2027 list also picks Bolivia and Quito.
travel.you: Pay in the local currency when a card terminal offers dollars, and use a card with no foreign transaction fee.

picks.title: What Should My Children Do?
picks.text: An economist asks what the next generation should learn, and what it should stop worrying about, in a world changed by AI. Useful for any family planning school or career choices.

picks.title: Primetime Preacher$
picks.text: A 113 minute film on Jim Bakker, Jerry Falwell and Jimmy Swaggart, three 1980s televangelists who built TV ministries before scandal. A sharp look at how money flows when trust is the product.

items.text: NASA ran a developmental RS-25 Moon rocket engine for its full 200 seconds at Stennis Space Center.
Scientists found bacteria that removed about 98% of radioactive promethium-147 in 60 hours.
India declared at 720 for 9 in Wellington, the highest Test innings ever made in New Zealand.
NASA's Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth.
BepiColombo is entering orbit around Mercury, only the second spacecraft ever to do so.
ESA's Hera is arriving at the asteroid Didymos to study the crater from NASA's DART impact.
Artemis II splashed down off San Diego after a 10 day trip around the Moon, the first crewed lunar voyage in more than 50 years.
NASA's Perseverance set the record for distance driven on another world, more than 45 km on Mars.
The Hubble Space Telescope completed its 200,000th orbit of Earth.
